03 Request flow — the main path

Trace one representative request end-to-end: {{POST /orders}}. Show where it can be rejected and where side-effects fire.

flowchart TD
    S(["Request arrives
{{METHOD /path}}"]) --> AUTH{"Valid session / token?"}
    AUTH -->|no| R401["401 Unauthorized"]
    AUTH -->|yes| AUTHZ{"Allowed to do this?
see § Permissions"}
    AUTHZ -->|no| R403["403 Forbidden"]
    AUTHZ -->|yes| VAL{"Payload valid?"}
    VAL -->|no| R400["400 + field errors"]
    VAL -->|yes| BIZ["{{Apply business rules}}"]
    BIZ --> TX["{{Write in one transaction}}"]
    TX --> EVT[["{{Emit event / enqueue job}}"]]
    TX --> OK(["{{201 Created}}"])
    EVT -.-> WK["{{Worker picks it up}}
see § Background work"]

    class AUTH,AUTHZ,VAL decision
    class R401,R403,R400 deny

04 Permissions & access model

Who can do what, and exactly where that decision is made in code. Every "it depends" in the matrix gets a footnote.

Roles

{{admin}}

{{Full control. Granted by …}}

{{editor}}

{{Create and change own resources. Granted by …}}

{{viewer}}

{{Read-only. Default for new accounts.}}

{{service}}

{{Machine identity for integrations. API key scoped to …}}

Permission matrix

Action{{admin}}{{editor}}{{viewer}}{{service}}Enforced in
{{Read resource}}✓✓✓✓{{policy.ts#canRead}}
{{Create resource}}✓✓✗¹{{policy.ts#canCreate}}
{{Edit resource}}✓²✗✗{{policy.ts#canEdit}}
{{Delete resource}}✓✗✗✗{{policy.ts#canDelete}}
{{Manage users / roles}}✓✗✗✗{{admin/routes.ts}}

¹ {{Only with the write scope on the API key.}}   ² {{Only resources they own, or in a workspace they belong to.}}

Authorization decision

The exact order checks run in. If this diagram and the code disagree, the code is the bug or this is — fix one today.

flowchart TD
    IN(["Request + identity"]) --> T{"Token / session valid?"}
    T -->|"no or expired"| D401["Deny · 401"]
    T -->|yes| SA{"Is service account?"}
    SA -->|yes| SC{"Key has required scope?"}
    SC -->|no| D403a["Deny · 403
missing scope"]
    SC -->|yes| RL
    SA -->|no| ROLE{"Role permits action?
(matrix above)"}
    ROLE -->|no| D403b["Deny · 403"]
    ROLE -->|"admin"| RL
    ROLE -->|"editor / viewer"| OWN{"Owns resource or
member of its workspace?"}
    OWN -->|no| D403c["Deny · 403
not owner"]
    OWN -->|yes| RL{"Within rate limit?"}
    RL -->|no| D429["Deny · 429"]
    RL -->|yes| AL["Audit-log the decision"]
    AL --> OK(["Allow → handler"])

    class IN actor
    class T,SA,SC,ROLE,OWN,RL decision
    class D401,D403a,D403b,D403c,D429 deny
    class AL service
    class OK allow

06 Background work & integrations

Anything that happens without a user waiting on it. Show retries and the dead-letter path — that's where incidents come from.

flowchart LR
    EV[["{{order.created}}"]] --> W["{{Worker}}"]
    W --> X{"{{Third-party}} call ok?"}
    X -->|yes| DONE(["Mark synced"])
    X -->|"no, retryable"| RT{"Attempts < {{5}}?"}
    RT -->|yes| BK["Backoff {{2^n s}}"] --> W
    RT -->|no| DLQ[("Dead-letter queue")]
    DLQ --> ALERT["🚨 Page {{on-call}}"]
    X -->|"no, permanent"| DLQ
